findings.title: Accidentally committed git submodule (gitlink) of the repository itself
findings.body: This PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing a gitlink entry (`Subproject commit a5d2909...`, which is the base commit of this very repository). There is no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry, so this is almost certainly an accidentally `git add`ed nested checkout rather than an intentional submodule. It pollutes the repository root, will show up as an unresolvable submodule for anyone cloning with `--recurse-submodules`, and can confuse tooling and CI. It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Substring match treats negated/excluded error queries as error-focused
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a naive substring check: `if "event.type:error" in query`. A discover query like `!event.type:error` (transactions only) still contains that substring, so the function returns True and `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count` (sum of `sample_weight`) even though the query explicitly excludes error events and transactions don't carry `sample_weight`. The same applies to queries where `event.type:error` appears inside a quoted message or tag value, or alongside `OR event.type:transaction`. Consequence: silently wrong (under/over-counted or zeroed) results returned to users. The check should parse the search query and verify a positive `event.type:error` filter rather than substring matching.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility checked against outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` uses the closure variable `dataset` (the dataset chosen for the overall request) rather than the `scoped_dataset` argument that the query is actually executed against. In the dashboard-widget split path, `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `split_dataset = discover` and an errors-only query even when the outer dataset is a metrics/performance dataset — in that case `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(metrics_performance, ...)` returns False, so the errors-only split query never gets the upsampling transform. The result is that error counts in split dashboard widgets are reported as raw counts while the same data queried directly is upsampled, producing inconsistent numbers.

findings.title: Eligibility inspects raw request query instead of the query actually being executed
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` calls `_is_error_focused_query(request)`, which reads `request.GET.get("query")`. However, `_get_event_stats` receives a `query` string that is rewritten before execution in several paths — e.g. the dashboard-split logic builds `errors_only_query = f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` and `transactions_only_query = f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"`. Because the helper ignores the effective query string, the upsampling decision is based on the original user query: the transactions-only split query can get the `count() -> sum(sample_weight)` transform applied (wrong results, since transactions have no `sample_weight`), and the errors-only split query can miss it when the original query didn't literally contain `event.type:error`. The effective query string should be threaded through to the check.

findings.title: Python built-in `hash()` used in a shared cache key
findings.body: The cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}"`. Using Python's built-in `hash()` for a cache key is fragile: it can collide for different project sets (a collision would make one set of projects inherit the cached allowlist decision of a different set, silently enabling or disabling upsampling for 60s), and its value is not guaranteed stable across Python builds/platforms, which defeats sharing the cache across heterogeneous deployments. A deterministic serialization (e.g. `-`.join of sorted ids, or a hashlib digest) should be used instead.

findings.title: Docstring contradicts the caching behavior of the caller
findings.body: The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` states: "This function reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... This is intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state." In practice the only production caller, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, wraps it in a 60-second cache and also provides `invalidate_upsampling_cache`, which is never called from anywhere in the codebase. The documented guarantee is therefore false, and allowlist changes are silently stale for up to a minute with no wired-up invalidation path. Either wire up invalidation or correct the docstring.
